text: You already know SQL and SOQL, so SAQL should feel familiar. It is close, but not the same. In this lesson we ask one question in all three languages, then pull out the differences that matter.

Here is the question: which stages have the most opportunities? In SQL, it is one statement. Select the stage and a count, from the table, group by stage, order by the count descending, and limit to ten. In SQL Server, TOP would replace limit.

In SOQL it is almost the same. Select the stage and count the Ids, from the Opportunity object, group, order, and limit. The difference is what it queries: live Salesforce objects, subject to Salesforce query limits.
In SAQL, the same logic becomes a sequence. Load the dataset. Group by stage. Then foreach generate the columns. Order and limit. Each line takes a stream and hands a new one to the next.

Four differences to remember. First, order: SAQL is a pipeline, and where you place a filter changes its meaning. Second, grouping and output are separate statements. Third, joins become cogroups, which group first, so you lose row-level grain. And fourth, SAQL queries prepared datasets, not live data, so results are only as fresh as the last load.
